title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Witch of Izalith** or simply **Izalith** (イザリス) is a mentioned character in *Dark Souls*. She is also mentioned in *Dark Souls II*, although by that time her name is lost to history and only her nickname of "mother of pyromancy" remains.

A legendary fire sorcerer who found one of the four Lord Souls, she helped bring an end to the Age of Ancients and the rule of the dragons to establish the Age of Fire, and established an underground civilization named after her. She had many daughters, nicknamed the "Daughters of Chaos", which included Quelaag, Quelana and "The Fair Lady", as well as a son. By the time of the game's events, her magical experiments backfired, fusing her soul and two of her daughters' into a new horrible being, the Bed of Chaos. Although the Bed was eventually slain by the Chosen Undead and its soul fed to the Lordvessel, fragments of the Witch's soul survived.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : The name of the Witch is literally **Izalith**, as stated by Quelana in the Japanese version, where she calls the Witch "my mother Izalith".
During her dialogue, Quelana mentions that most humans are unable to perceive her, and implies that they absolutely cannot, so long as she actively does not want them to.
Despite herself being consumed by the Chaos Flame, Izalith was partially successful in replicating the First Flame. Not only does Chaos generate life, it also has its own fire-linking quality, wherein a demon Champion is destined to rekindle it, becoming the Demon Prince. This system parallels the prophecy of the Chosen Undead and their becoming a Lord of Cinder.

title: Lost Izalith
snippet:
Lost Izalith -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : Izalith was once the domain of the Witch of Izalith, and was seemingly a great and booming city. However, when The Witch attempted to recreate the First Flame from her own Lord Soul, she failed to control it and was transformed into the Bed of Chaos. Izalith was subsequently overrun by the demons born from the Bed of Chaos. The demons fought against Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and his knights, were defeated, and after hearing Quelaag's cut dialogue, were apparently punished by being contained to their fallen city.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the times and region of Lothric, both the bed and the flame have gone out, and the demons are now a dying species, as no new members of their race are being generated. Some remain in a secret city of demons, found amidst Izalith's decrepit structures, most of its citizens being demons and corrupted Izalith citizens. The Old Demon King sits alone amidst fallen combatants, with his flames dying out, the last of the original citizens of Izalith to have remembered the birth of Chaos, and the Witch of Izalith.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: Ages after her Lord Soul was used to link the First Flame, Izalith's very name was lost. In the region of Drangleic, only few remained who remembered her—only that she was the mother of pyromancy, and that she was devoured by her chaos flame. However, some remnants of her soul manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_i 
 dark_souls_i : Quelana was originally a "flame witch" who used fire sorcery. When Izalith was consumed and the demons infested the city, she fled and became the creator of pyromancy. It is unknown whether the knowledge of fire sorcery was forgotten by her or whether she created pyromancy as a safer version of it. Quelana passed on her knowledge to Salaman, who in turn passed on his knowledge of pyromancy to the people of the Great Swamp.

According to a developer interview, Quelana and the other Daughters of Chaos are a different species than humans, despite being similar in appearance. Her in-game model may not reflect her "canon" appearance, with pale, ash-colored skin, as seen in the opening cutscene and achievement art.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : Quelaag is a daughter of the Witch of Izalith and, along with most of her family, failed to escape from the chaotic flame and was corrupted by it. Due to exposure to the flame, Quelaag and her sister mutated into spider-like creatures with their upper body being fused to the monsters' backs.

title: Lore
snippet: The Age of Fire began prosperous and rich, but soon the fires started to go out again and with them the power of the Lords. In an effort to prolong Age of Fire, the Witch of Izalith tried to recreate the First Flame, but the experiment failed and a flame called "The Flame of Chaos" is created instead, which transformed her into the Bed of Chaos and many creatures into the demons that roam Lordran. Her children are transformed as well, with her son becoming a flame demon called Ceaseless Discharge and her daughter Quelaag and her sister partially into spiders. Her followers stay loyal to her, however, and become known as the "Witches of Chaos". Only her daughter, Quelana, escaped the fire and becomes the mother of pyromancy. This being said, Mother Izalith did eventually *succeed* in stabilizing the Chaos Flame with 2 of her sisters.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - the_witch_of_izalith 
 the_witch_of_izalith : The Witch used the power of her Lord Soul to weave great storms of fire against the Everlasting Dragons. She passed fragments of this soul to her children, the Daughters of Chaos, and her only son. Like her children, she had ashen skin and blue lips, though she stood much taller than them and seems to be of identical height to the staves her children used for flame sorcery.

As the fires faded, she tried to create a new flame to replicate the First Flame, but it backfired and ended up costing her life, and gave birth to the race of demons. Her children were also corrupted, except for Quelana, who taught a flame manipulating art to a human and became the mother of pyromancy. Many years later, the demons began to die out, as the flame of chaos began to fade much like the First Flame did.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Ceaseless Discharge
snippet: Around the same time, Izalith was experimenting with her Lord Soul and the power of fire and souls and at a certain point, driven by ambition and arrogance, she tried to create a "First Flame" of her own, using her own Lord Soul as a basis to make a power similar to the primordial force that had brought life into the world. The experiment, however, was not entirely successful because the result was a Flame of Chaos, an unstable power that the witch was unable to control. Izalith herself was initially consumed by it and became a beast of chaos fire along with two of her daughters in the process transforming themselves into a "Bed of Chaos". This creature, fueled by the power of the Flame of Chaos, became a seebed for a new life form: Demons.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - description 
 description : Izalith appears as a towering humanoid, visibly taller than both her children and their catalysts. She has blue lips, ashen skin and hands burnt from extracting her soul from the First Flame. She wears a much more refined version of the gold-hemmed black robes her children wear.

title: Chaos (mechanic)
snippet:
Chaos (mechanic) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients, the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great and powerful firestorms. At the time, the Witch and her followers were powerful flame sorcerers who lived in the city of Izalith. Blacksmiths of the ancient city crafted powerful weapons using Chaos arts. Thus, during the earliest known ages of the world, Chaos developed its reputation as a powerful force.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

title: Demon Firesage
snippet: lore : The Firesage Demons were the first generation of demons spawned from the Bed of Chaos, the entity that appeared following the attempt of the Witch of Izalith to make a power similar to the First Flame using her Lord Soul. The attempt was successful and she create the Flame of Chaos but Izalith and her powerful soul became a seedbed for a new lifeform: the mother and source of all demons. While the very first demon, Ceaseless Discharge, was a monstrous and unstable mutation of a son of Izalith while her newly created Flame of Chaos was still unstable, the Firesage Demon is one of the demons that were generated after Izalith and her daughters managed to stabilize their new flame, thus gaining a more defined body and control over the power of chaos inside its body. These new creatures learned to coexist with the already present society of Izalith, becoming "demon priests" of the Flame of Chaos and Izalith and even going as far as to learn the primordial flame sorceries developed

title: Old Ones
snippet:
Old Ones -  Dark Souls II - boss - the_lost_sinner_witch_of_izalith 
 the_lost_sinner_witch_of_izalith : The Lost Sinner, wielder of the Old Witch Soul, is burdened by her past misdeeds. In the same manner, the Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate the First Flame using her Lord Soul, but instead created the Flame of Chaos. Other correlations that can be pointed are the creature similar to a Chaos Bug seen crawling into the eyehole of the Lost Sinner’s mask, her Handcuffs having the power to augment pyromancy and the phantoms of Pyromancers that aid her in battle in NG+.

Shalquoir comments "Trying to light the First Flame", and again it's hard to say if she's referring to the Sinner or the Witch possessing her.

Second Playthroughs and onward will cause the Lost Sinner to drop the Old Witch Soul.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet:
The Old Chaos -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : In ancient times, the Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate the First Flame with the Lord Soul that was in her possession. Instead, she spawned a corrupted fire known as the Flame of Chaos. When she failed to control the new flame, it consumed her and molded her into a twisted being known as the Bed of Chaos, the source of all demons.

Eventually, the Bed of Chaos was destroyed by the Chosen Undead, but the flames of Chaos lived on. At an unknown point, the flames of Chaos were discovered deep below the kingdom of Eleum Loyce. In an attempt to appease the raging flame, the Ivory King built a great cathedral at its mouth and the oracle of Eleum Loyce, Alsanna, prayed in silent vigilance. The attempt was unsuccessful and the flames still raged.

title: Chaos Storm
snippet:
Chaos Storm -  Dark Souls - spell - description 
 description : Art of the Flame of Chaos, which engulfed the Witch of Izalith and her daughters. Erects localized chaos fire pillars.

The Witch of Izalith, in an ambitious attempt to copy the First Flame, created instead the Flame of Chaos, a twisted bed of life.

title: Pyromancy (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Pyromancy (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - lore 
 lore : Before the creation of Pyromancy, flame sorceries were used by the Witch of Izalith, her Daughters of Chaos, and they later taught it to the Demon Firesages. The Witch and her daughters used flame sorcery to challenge the ancient dragons, casting it from catalysts just as soul sorceries were. In the wake of her attempt to recreate the First Flame, the Witch of Izalith and some of her daughters were engulfed in the newly formed Bed of Chaos. The witches mastered the power of the Flame of Chaos and gave birth to the Pyromancy and all knowledge of flame sorcery has since vanished.

Quelana of Izalith, a Daughter of Chaos, managed to flee the catastrophe created by her mother. Quelana, who is credited as one of the "mothers of pyromancy", after escaping from Izalith, teaches her art to a select few students and now resides in Blighttown.

title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
Flame of Chaos -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Flame of Chaos was created by the Witch of Izalith when she attempted to use her Lord Soul to recreate the First Flame. When she was unable to control it, she was consumed by it and transformed into the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons. Most of her children were similarly consumed and transformed into monstrosities; her daughter Quelana, however, escaped and used the Flame of Chaos to create the art of Pyromancy.

After the defeat of the Bed of Chaos at the hand of the Chosen Undead, the flames of Chaos persisted. It would eventually be discovered beneath Eleum Loyce, in the form of The Old Chaos. The Old Chaos would go on to consume many of Eleum Loyce's knights, turning them into Charred Loyce Knights, and eventually claiming the ruler of Eleum Loyce himself. The Ivory King would eventually be freed, at the bequest of his oracle Alsanna, by the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : After The Witch of Izalith found an immense and powerful Lord Soul near the First Flame, she pooled her and her daughters' newfound strength into aiding fellow Lords in winning the war against the Dragons and built their civilization underground. They continued to experiment with the power of fire and souls; at a certain point, driven by ambition and arrogance, Izalith, using her own Lord Soul as a basis, tried to recreate the First Flame, the primordial force that had brought life into the world. This, however, was not entirely successful, resulting in the Flame of Chaos, an unstable power that the witch was unable to control. She was initially consumed by it and became a beast of chaos fire along with two of her daughters: the "Bed of Chaos". This creature, fueled by the power of the Flame of Chaos, became a seedbed for a new life form: Demons.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_first_flame 
 the_first_flame : The advent of fire occurred, and with it came heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. The First Flame was born, source of all fire. However, from the dark came humanoid creatures - Hollows. These creatures found the Lord Souls near the flames and took on the powers they gave. They were:
Gravelord Nito, The First of the Dead, who offered much of his own soul to death, granting him the ability to administer the death of all life.
The Witch of Izalith, who became the leader of the flame sorcerers, later the so-called "Daughters of Chaos".
Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, who was to achieve great things in his life.
A fourth unique Lord Soul called the "Dark Soul" was found by the Furtive Pygmy, who is the ancestor of the humans. They are supposed to bring about the Age of Dark, in which humanity rules the world. A distant descendant of him is the Chosen Undead.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : She is the Fair Lady's older sister. When their mother, the Witch of Izalith along with their other two sisters became the Bed of Chaos, she and her sister became half demon spiders.

Quelaag and her sister stationed just outside the Demon Ruins, in a fraction of Blighttown that became known as Quelaag's Domain. The two started to breed demon insects to enlarge the demon army, by offering Humanities to the Fair Lady. People in Blighttown venerated the two witches, and gladly accepted to become hosts of the Fair Lady's eggs.

When the people were stricken by a blight, Quelaag's sister chose to absorb their pus to save their lives, which greatly weakened and blinded her while making any further eggs incapable of holding life. Quelaag remained by her side as her guardian and a hunter of undead to gather the humanity necessary to sustain her sister as a Fire Keeper.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - the_fast_fading_flame_and_the_birth_of_chaos 
 the_fast_fading_flame_and_the_birth_of_chaos : Gwyn found one day that the First Flame was fading, and that once it had burnt out the Age of Dark would begin.

The Lords feared the Dark, and sought to prolong the Age of Fire. The Witch of Izalith attempted to create a new flame. However, this new Chaos Flame grew out of control and consumed the Witch of Izalith and many of her children, soon forming into a creation known as the Bed of Chaos, which consumed Izalith and mutated most of the Witch of Izalith's remaining children into abominable creatures, while also turning her only son into a volcanic monstrosity. From the Chaos Flame came the race of Demons, against which Gwyn waged war. The Silver Knights that fought in this war were scorched and became the Black Knights.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : As of the time of Lothric, the primal pyromancies of Quelana and her mother were near-consigned to legend among contemporary pyromancers. Izalith's pyromancies were said to only be known to old Master Salaman, mentioned by Quelana as being her pupil, now lost to time. Even as her pyromancies themselves were all but history, her cautionary tales on the dangers of the flame were passed down through generations of pyromancers.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who was tasked with sacrificing himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Despite the Bed of Chaos having been destroyed by a Chosen Undead, a fragment of the Flames of Chaos managed to survive and drifted to settle underground in the far north of Drangleic. Here it reformed as an expanse of fire, lava and roots and started to give birth to atrocities and monsters that cursed the region, leading people to flee in fear. Eventually the Ivory King and his knights managed to eliminate the demons that arose from the Old Chaos and drive them back into the depths. The sovereign, thanks to the power of his soul, thus built the kingdom of Eleum Loyce over that land and erected an immense cathedral, a fortress city and a Garrison Wall above the Chaos, in an attempt to contain it and its horrors with all his efforts, even going so far as to use the power of his own soul to stem his raging flames.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: At some point, a pyromancer was imprisoned inside the furthest cell of the Sinners' Rise, an isolated tower apart from the The Lost Bastille. While the Bastille was used to contain the Undead that plagued the region, this pyromancer was imprisoned and contained in an extreme manner, with Penal Handcuffs to restrain their powers and a Penal Mask with spikes pointing inward to bind and torture them, to be punished for their sins. One day the prisoner came into contact with the soul of Izalith deep inside the Lost Bastille, and a Chaos Bug similar to one Izalith had been reduced came to inhabit their body. The remnants of Izalith's will influenced the prisoner, leaving them eternally to punish themselves for the sins of her past, for trying to light a First Flame in her arrogance. Their sword became cursed with a power similar to that of the ancient Chaos Blade, symbolizing the burden of Izalith's misdeeds.

title: Ceaseless Discharge
snippet:
Ceaseless Discharge -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : Ceaseless Discharge is the youngest child and only known son of the Witch of Izalith. However he was born with sores inflamed by the lava flowing in Izalith and so his older sisters, the witches of Izalith, gave him a magical ring to ease his pain.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : The kingdom of Lordran was established, and the Lords took to their different homes and agendas. Gwyn had his city of the gods, Anor Londo, built in the center of Lordran, which would eventually be inhabited by his children, his faithful Silver Knights, and other members of his clan. These include other deities, such as the king's four knights.

Seath was awarded dukedom, even receiving a fragment of Gwyn's soul, and was rewarded with an archive. He retreated into his new home to study immortality, through the Primordial Crystal, and his discoveries would inspire scholars to pursue Seath's art of Sorcery as a result of this. He also bequeathed fragments to four humans, and naming them rulers of New Londo, for their foresight.

The Witch established the civilization of Izalith underground and continued to experiment with fire sorcery.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. title: Lords

Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - age_of_disparity 
 age_of_disparity : Little is known of the lives of the Lords before the discovery of Fire. Gwyn had an uncle in Allfather Lloyd, and The Witch was accompanied by her adult daughters when she claimed her soul, so it is possible they may have existed before claiming their Lord Souls.

title: Zullie the Witch
snippet:
Zullie the Witch -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Zullie was a heretical sorceress, denoted by her title of witch and the pointed hat that she wore with deep, yet unspoken pride. Yet in spite of her confidence in the practice of witchcraft, she still had a need for hiding that part of her, especially when traveling. For that purpose she used a long veil.

She is best known for her role in the stories of Alva the Wayfarer, whom she set out to corrupt by all means necessary once she learned of his deep dedication to Saint Serreta. However, after her many failed attempts to seduce the knight, she would change her ways and become a valuable ally to Alva, supporting him in his endeavors and staying by his side even when he was consumed with regret and self-loathing for failing his mission.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - other_known_unkindled 
 other_known_unkindled : Sister Friede, formerly known as **Elfriede**. It is unclear when she was resurrected and whether or not it happened in relation to Lothric. In her first life, she was the leader of the Sable Church of Londor, which aims to end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark; as such, she might have aimed to seize the First Flame rather than to link it. In her second life, Elfriede, now renamed Friede, renounced her past, instead making a home in the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Gold-Hemmed Black Cloak
snippet:
Gold-Hemmed Black Cloak -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : Worn by the witch Quelana of Izalith, mother of pyromancy and Daughter of Chaos.

She wore this gold-hemmed black cloak before even the Age of Fire, and it offers strong resistance versus fire, poison, and other perils.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_war_of_fire 
 the_war_of_fire : With their new found power the Lords challenged the dominion of the Everlasting Dragons over the World. The Lords allied with one of the dragons, Seath the Scaleless, who sought the immortal scales of the dragons and thus betrayed his own kind. A very long and destructive war was begun by the Lords and their amassed armies. Gwyn used his powerful bolts to peel their stone scales, while the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms against them and finally the Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death upon the dragons. The war was won by the Lords and the dragons were defeated. A golden Age of Fire begun as the World rebuilt under the new rule of the now as deities perceived Lords.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: At one point Izalith, aiming to gain greater sway over the Flame of Chaos, lost all control of the power again and never regained it: Chaos engulfed the Lord and her daughters before scorching their city with them. Izalith and her two daughters directly involved in the experiment were left permanently scarred, reduced to a monstrous lignified creature anchored in the throne room at the center of the city. Of the daughters of Izalith, few managed to escape. Quelaag and her sister's lower bodies were molded into deformed demonic spiders and the flames of chaos engulfed them but they managed to escape the city and survive on its borders, carving out a domain for themselves. The only other survivor, who managed to avoid the corruption of chaos and retain a normal body, was Quelana, who remained in self-imposed exile around the ruins of her country for centuries.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet: The victory of the Lords in the war marked the end of the Age of Ancients and the beginning of the Age of Fire.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Souls of Lords -  Dark Souls - item - lore 
 lore : The Souls of Lords were discovered by the chosen few that "came from the dark". Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Nito, the First of the Dead, The Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

Gwyn, Nito and The Witch of Izalith used the power procured from the Lord Souls to challenge the Everlasting Dragons for dominion of the world and, with the help of others, were successful in their endeavor.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate her own First Flame by using her Lord Soul, but this resulted in her own demise and the creation of the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons, who inherited possession of the Soul.

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards are fragments of Gwyn's Lord Soul and were bestowed as gifts. One was given to Seath the Scaleless for betraying his own kind. Another was given to the Four Kings when Lord Gwyn recognized their foresight as leaders of New Londo.

 lead : **Chaos Witch Quelaag** (混沌の魔女クラーグ) is a boss in *Dark Souls*.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Although the lower half of their bodies were transformed into a chaos spider, Quelaag and her sister managed to carve out a domain for themselves on the edge of the realm of Izalith, near what was called Blighttown. While the older Quelaag maintained control over their refuge thanks to her strength, the younger one, who was a Fire Keeper with an immense amount of humanity within her, began producing eggs by the dozen, until they covered their entire lair. In time, the Undead exiled to the depths of the Undead Burg and who had ended up in the rotten Blighttown chose to serve the Flame of Chaos and the two demonic daughters of Izalith of their own free will.

 age_of_fire : In the aftermath of the war, The Age of Fire came about, bringing an age of sunlight and prosperity. The Everlasting Dragons were all but extinct, but the race has many descendants throughout the world, some greater and some lesser, with varying degrees of similarity to their progenitors.

title: Zullie the Witch
snippet:
Zullie the Witch -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Tales and songs of Alva's exploits and travels still persist in the era of Lothric, and with him the figures of Zullie and Serreta. Sadly, those stories tend to end in tragedy.

It can be surmised that Zullie's end was also quite tragic, as a corpse with the entirety of her set can be found in the Ringed City, guarded by the very knight that had given her life meaning long ago. Yet the witch cannot simply rest either, seeing as her spirit is summoned by the Judicator Giants who preside over the legendary city. Since her body lay abandoned unceremoniously in a corner of the city, it's unlikely that she befriended the wizened beings the way Silver Knight Ledo did long ago, so she was probably forced into the role like the ancient company of knights that came before her, as punishment for her trespass.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Bed of Chaos** (混沌の苗床) is a boss in *Dark Souls*. A hideous lifeform which the Witch of Izalith has turned into, it is found in what remains of her land, Lost Izalith. It is a "puzzle boss" with unconventional mechanics.

Although the traditional way of reaching the Bed involves slaying both the Demon Firesage and the Centipede Demon, a shortcut can be opened by offering Quelaag's Sister 30 Humanity through the Chaos Servant covenant.

After a while, she asks the player to defeat what is left of her corrupted sisters, Quelaag and the Daughter of Chaos, and the Bed of Chaos to free the consumed souls of her mother and sisters. Upon completing her requests, she gifts the player her final pyromancy: Fire Tempest.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder

These developments pushed Gwyn to wage war against the chaos demons, developing weapons and fighting techniques strong enough to face their sizable new enemies and sending his Silver Knights to Izalith, in a war where their armor and weapons were charred black. Gwyn's knights fell short of total victory, unable to exterminate the demons or destroy the Bed of Chaos, and ended up retreating and only managing to banish the demons underground while enslaving some lesser demons who would become

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: The first demon who manifested itself was the youngest son of Izalith. He was a younger brother of the other witches who gifted him a magic ring to negate his pain from the lava sores that tortured him. However, the still-unstable Flame of Chaos led him to transform into a monstrous demon and drop his ring, leaving the flames of chaos to burn him constantly as he couldn't control them, while also generating another distorted Centipede Demon. Despite becoming the first distorted creature created by the Flame of Chaos, at a certain point Izalith and her daughters managed to stabilize the new power they had created and began to generate the first real demons: life forms with stable bodies and capable of controlling the flame of chaos within each of them. title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance.

snippet: This was once the home to the daughters of the Witch of Izalith and the demons born from the Flame of Chaos. Unlike the First Flame, which is tied to the souls of the undead, the faded Flame of Chaos was tied to the souls of the demons, and so the lifeless bodies of Capra, Taurus, Asylum and a single Centipede Demon can be found strewn throughout the ruins and piled high near the Old Demon King, one of the last remaining demons of old. A petrified arachnoid body, resembling Quelaag's Sister, lies within the ruins, where a humanoid corpse holds the Quelana Pyromancy Tome, indicated that the sisters lived here at one point.

snippet: lore : Elfriede is the eldest sister of Yuria and Liliane. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. title: Elizabeth
snippet:
Elizabeth -  Dark Souls II - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Elizabeth is a member of the Mushroom People of the adjacent woods. She is a master of golden sorcery and the guardian of Oolacile's Sanctuary, as well as Princess Dusk's wet nurse. The two appear to be very close, as the princess will tell her about the Chosen Undead, who rescued her from her imprisonment in the Golden Crystal Golem. She is also adept in medicine, treating mushrooms into potent restorative items.

When the Chosen Undead is dragged into the past by Manus, she is able to instantly recognize them due to the stories of Dusk. She begs for their help and shares her insight and wares with them. She speaks of Knight Artorias, and how he would fall to the Abyss, and of Marvelous Chester, another man from a faraway time who she describes as being odious.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even eons past the first linking of the Flame, Kaathe didn't stop trying to bring the Age of Dark. The serpent took into his service what would become the three sisters at the helm of the Sable Church of Londor: Liliane, Yuria and Elfriede. He then directed their efforts to create a realm inhabited by Hollows that could offer salvation to them. Kaathe taught them his dark powers, and Londor carried out experiments aimed at understanding the Darksign and the Dark Soul under his watch. Their goal evolved into usurping the First Flame, tearing it from its Kiln and ensuring that it could be wielded to finally create a new Age of Man. To this end, the Sable Church awaited the arrival of a chosen Unkindled, preparing to assist and guide them to ensure that they succeeded in their goal. However, before he could see his dream of an Age of Dark realized, Kaathe died of unknown causes, leaving the three sisters to continue to lead Londor and await the future Dark Lord.

title: Archtree
snippet: At some point the creatures that found the Lord Souls near the First Flame underground and developed their powers emerged to the surface with the intention of exterminating the Dragons and conquer the world for themselves. During the war that followed, Izalith and her daughters used sorcery and their powers to manipulate flames and weaved great firestorms that scorched the very earth, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons and Gwyn and his knights battled the dragons with their their mighty lightning bolts. After the long struggle the Lords emerged victorious, exterminating most of the archdragons and archtrees, thus conquering the surface world for themselves.

title: Jugo
snippet:
Also in Jugo was a particular group made up mostly of women known as the Desert Sorceresses. These were skilled pyromancers who utilized "flame fans" rather than basic pyromancy flames, suggesting an ability to exploit their country's arid climate to generate fire spells through unconventional sorcery catalysts. They were known for their thin clothing permeated with magic whose revealing nature effectively served as a means to distract weak-willed enemies, helping the sorceresses even enthrall them into their service. At some point after the fall of Vendrick's kingdom, a group of these sorceresses from Jugo moved into Drangleic and settled into the domain of Queen Mytha near the Earthen Peak and Harvest Valley.

A descendant of the Desert Sorceresses of Earthen Peak, Zoey, survived into the end of the Age of Fire. Unlike her predecessors, Zoey did not use her beauty to poison others, instead becoming a queen of sorts to the feeble ones.

title: Lothric
snippet: During the founding of Lothric, the First Flame drifted north towards the kingdom, forever marking the history and culture of its people. Due the presence of the Flame, the lands of the world began a geographical and temporal drift towards the city of Lothric, owing to the space-time altering effects of **Convergence.****** One or more Primordial Serpents developed an interest in propagating the cult of Firelinking within Lothric, to uphold the Age of Fire and the tradition started with Gwyn's sacrifice. Eventually Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city. Over time, serpents passed on the Firelinking culture to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to uphold the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Primordial serpents were depicted in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angelic wings, showing their central role within the kingdom and their perception as divine

At one point they reached the Undead Crypt and were welcomed into the it by the Fenito, ending up residing in the crypt beside them, collaborating with them in their tasks and sharing their power of death. title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet: Velka is a peculiar deity who is addressed as a "witch" and "heretic deity"; although she remains in the Anor Londo pantheon, her ideas and practices deviate from dominant tenets. She is involved with secret rituals capable of denying the use of magic in an area, as well as sacrificial rituals for creating mystical rings, and the talismans crafted with her hair are used to cast miracles drawing not upon faith but intelligence, implying that the goddess favors the latter among her followers. Velka is nonetheless greatly influential in the world of men and of gods, and is versed in arts both new and old, given her interest in the most recent sorceries.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Bed of Chaos, still fused with her two daughters and her original body reduced to that of a Chaos Bug under all her roots. The Chosen Undead thus challenged and killed her to obtain her powerful Lord Soul. The destruction of the original Flame of Chaos ended Izalith's misery, but it also marked the beginning of the end for the demons who, without the Bed of Chaos that had spawned them, became a dying race.

title: Londor
snippet: The three sisters shared Kaathe's aim of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark; however, the means and the ultimate goal differed from Kaathe's original vision. The sisters of Londor sought to crown not a "Lord of Men", but instead a "Lord of Hollows", who they claimed would wear "the true face of man". By the time of the Sable Church, the form of the Hollow appears to have been acknowledged as the original condition, the "most honest shape", of humans; whether this position was espoused by Kaathe himself is uncertain. Moreover, instead of leaving the First Flame to die out, the Sable Church wished for their Lord of Hollows to usurp the Flame, to "wrest it from its mantle", which would empower their new Lord. This mission seems to align with Vendrick's own wisdom, who viewed a true leader as one who would "inherit fire and harness the dark". title: Fire Witch
snippet:
Fire Witch -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Fire Witches use several different pyromancies that can cause heavy damage if the player is caught in them. They will usually switch between conjuring a trail of fire directly at the player or creating a single pillar of flame under their feet. Both of these attacks can be used from a long distance and can hit the player even if they are behind cover.

These enemies often appear with Pontiff Knights and Irithyllian Slaves, which makes them challenging to engage directly. It is recommended to take out the accompanying foes before dealing with the Witches themselves, as the player can easily be staggered by other attacks, leaving them open to the Witch's pyromancy.

title: Londor
snippet:
At some point before seeing his dream realized, Kaathe died, and left the sisters of the Sable Church to carry on his vision of an Age of Dark led by the Dark Lord.

At some point, Elfriede, as leader of the Sable Church, departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, bringing the Sable Church's efforts to fruition, or if she wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose (see Sister Friede#Theories). Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash. Following her failure—and after being resurrected by the Bell of Awakening—Elfriede chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Having lost her purpose, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel and came to consider it her new home, leaving Yuria and Liliane to carry on the mission of Londor.

title: Gods
snippet: Rosaria, Goddess of Rebirth, a descendant of Gwynevere. She is a mute woman worshipped by the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, described outright as a Goddess and whom once possessed a sword shaped like a crescent moon reminiscent of the moon worshipped in Irithyll. She resides in a cathedral home to the heretic faith of the Deep, although her worship is separate from it, and possibly part of the Way of White.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
** The weapon skill of the Onyx Blade, "Elfriede's Blackflame", states that the blackflame was "born of the similarly-hued flame that smolders within her". Following from the speculation that Unkindled Ones lack the original Flame, this similarly-hued flame possibly hails from a different source, possibly the First Flame itself within the Kiln, the very fire which ended up burning Elfriede.
** Given the Sable Church's affinity with dark miracles, it seems likely that the First Flame would attempt to manifest within its would-be usurper as a derivation from these arts that are powered by the Darkness of humanity.

title: Unkindled
snippet: The Sable Church of Londor revere the Unkindled, as it is prophesied that an Unkindled will become the Lord of Hollows and bring about the Age of Dark. Elfriede, the eldest of the three sisters of the Sable Church, eventually departed Londor and attempted to link the Flame. The circumstances surrounding her departure are unclear; whether she intended to usurp the Flame or wholly abandoned Londor is uncertain. Regardless, she was unable to link the Flame, burned to Unkindled Ash. After her resurrection, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, a safe haven for the forlorn and the misshapen.

title: High Lord Wolnir
snippet: After falling into the Abyss, Wolnir discovered a form of pyromancy that used the darkness of humanity; these pyromancies seemed to seek a will of their own, a result of interacting with humanity. The pyromancers that had become the guardians of the catacombs would discover Wolnir's dark flame, born from the Abyss and shadowless, and employed it for their own usage.

title: Fire Witch Helm
snippet:
Fire Witch Helm -  Dark Souls III - armor - availability 
 availability : Dropped by Fire Witches in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley and Irithyll Dungeon.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Having secured absolute dominion over the world, Gwyn thus began the Age of Fire, a time of prosperity that was characterized by the power of the First Flame and the vision of the Great Lord. Gwyn's clan placed themselves atop the new world order, assuming the role of deities for humans who were their subjects, and Gwyn took the title "god of sunlight". Humans venerated the gods who lived in the city of Anor Londo in the region of Lordran, building an economy and culture around the use of souls, even hunting the descendants of dragons for sport and domesticating some of them. Gwyn left the other two Lords to tend to their own domains: Izalith built her civilization underground where she and her daughters continued to study flame sorcery, and Gravelord Nito remained in the Catacombs to oversee the dead.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_age_of_ancients 
 the_age_of_ancients : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

Before the Age of Fire was the Age of Ancients. It was a time in which the world was colorless and shrouded by fog. The land consisted of gray crags, archtrees and Everlasting Dragons, who were the rulers of the world. Humans and other creatures had yet to make an impression upon the world.

title: Dragon
snippet:
Dragon -  Dark Souls III - character - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : In the Age of Ancients, the world was shrouded by fog, filled with grey crags and arch-trees, and ruled by the immortal Everlasting Dragons. The dragons were unmatched, but eventually, subterranean humanoids would discover a great power within the First Flame, giving them the means to challenge the dragons.

With the birth of the First Flame—the Advent of Fire—the Lords challenged the ancient dragons for dominion of the world. Lord Gwyn's mighty bolts peeled apart their stone scales. The Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms, burning the Archtrees. Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death and disease.

title: Demon's Catalyst
snippet:
Demon's Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - description 
 description : Demon catalyst formed from Izalith molten rock. Can be used as fire weapon. The Demon Firesage was the first demon, and the last master of the original fire arts before the Witch of Izalith was engulfed by Chaos, creating pyromancy.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet:
Age of Ancients -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients the world was undistinguished and covered in fog: a land of gray rocks, great trees and everlasting dragons; everything was the same and time didn't exist.But at some point the First Flame appeared and brought "disparity" into the world, allowing the existence of everything and its opposite: heat and cold, life and death, light and dark.

It was during this time that the Lord Souls were found near the Flame. The three Lords who found them (Nito, Gwyn and the Witch of Izalith) formed a coalition and used the power of their newly discovered souls to challenge the Dragons, starting a very long and destructive war. However, there was a fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, which was found by the Furtive Pygmy. The only known act via this Lord was the fragmentation of their soul becoming the birth of Humanity, who would fight side by side with the Lords.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwynevere is the first daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. She was worshipped by the humans as the "goddess of sunlight" and a symbol of bounty and fertility, while she was also cherished by all the other gods. As a goddess of sunlight, her miracles of Bountiful Sunlight and Soothing Sunlight were able to convey the sun's rays to heal, a blessing she granted to many warriors. She also taught her miracles to her maidens and created holy water with healing properties thanks to her light. Gwynevere was venerated in a church alongside the main cathedral of Anor Londo; the structure was also used to contain the Painted World of Ariamis, protected by the Painting Guardians.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_age_of_fire 
 the_age_of_fire : After the defeat of the Everlasting Dragons Gwyn established the land of Lordran and granted Seath the title of "Duke" along with a part of his Lord Soul for his contribution in the war. He also gave another part of his Lord Soul as well as the titles of "King" to the Four Kings, the leaders of New Londo, in recognition of their foresight. Gwyn resided in the capital city of Anor Londo and had three children:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, Old God of War, who was stripped of his deific status and erased from history for his foolishness. He is closely related to the Warrior of Sunlight covenant and inherited the sunlight from his father. In an age long after this one, their identity was revealed to be the Nameless King.
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight, who later married Flame God Flann (and presumably left the land with him).
Dark Sun Gwyndolin, who was raised as a girl for his affection to the moon.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Nameless King is the firstborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshipped by humans as the "god of war".

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : Long ago, the world was an unformed, homogeneous place which lacked a true concept of disparity. The grey, rocky land was perpetually shrouded in fog, and the landscape was dominated by towering stone archtrees which extended into endless clouds. The everlasting dragons, ancient and immortal entities who transcended the later concepts of life and death, were the dominant beings. This period was known as the Age of Ancients.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Souls of Lords -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn bequeathed most of his power to the Gods, and burned as cinder for the First Flame, but even so, Lord Gwyn's soul is a powerful thing indeed.

Soul of the Bed of Chaos and the mother of all demons. This Lord Soul was found at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame from a soul, but instead created a distorted being of chaos and fire. Its power formed a bed of life which would become the source of all demons, and is more than enough to satiate the Lordvessel.

Soul of Gravelord Nito, first of the dead. This Lord Soul was discovered at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

Gravelord Nito administers the death of all manner of beings. The power of his soul is so great that it satiates the Lordvessel, despite the fact that much of its energy has already been offered to death.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. Should the Chosen Undead abandon the First Flame to die out after the defeat of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, they will "usher in the Age of Dark", and become the fabled "Dark Lord" of whom Kaathe speaks. It is important to note that Kaathe tells the Chosen Undead that the Age of Dark had apparently already begun shortly before Gwyn chose to link the Flame, though it was seemingly ended and replaced by the Age of Fire when the Flame was linked.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Demons** are a race in the *Dark Souls* universe.

"True" Demons (labelled **Chaos Demons** in this article), are beings (some unique, others members of specific sub-species) originating from the fall of Izalith prior to *Dark Souls*, during which the Witch of Izalith lost control of her Lord Soul, causing the creation of the Flame of Chaos that twisted beings in Izalith and turned the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, a creative force that kept on endlessly making new lifeforms: Demons, which spilled from Izalith into the world. title: Princess of Venn
snippet:
Princess of Venn -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The Princess of Venn was the heir to the throne of her kingdom. Her homeland despised the neighboring kingdom of Alken, and this feud was kept alive by both countries. Yet in spite of such deep-seated hatred, the young royal fell in love with the prince of the enemy kingdom, who himself felt the same way. Theirs was a forbidden love.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: When a Chosen Undead was able to ring the Bells of Awakening, overcome the challenges of Sen's Fortress and reach Anor Londo thus being rewarded with the Lordvessel, they would be guided by Kingseeker Frampt to find immense souls to fill the receptacle and link the fading First Flame to succeed Gwyn in his sacrifice. The Undead would thus have delved into the dangerous and pestilent Blighttown until they reached the edges of the ancient domain of Izalith. Here their path would be blocked by the half-demon daughter of Izalith Chaos Witch Quelaag but, after killing her, the Undead was able to gain access to the Demon Ruins. Making their way through the demons that infested the area, they reached the lost city of Izalith and the throne room where Izalith resided, having turned into the distorted Bed of Chaos, still fused with her two daughters and her original body reduced to that of a Chaos Bug under all her roots. The Chosen Undead thus challenged and killed her to obtain her powerful

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - later_gods_of_anor_londo 
 later_gods_of_anor_londo : Caitha, Goddess of Tears, who mourns the undeserving dead and the loved ones left behind. It is unclear whether she was already a Deity in the original pantheon of Anor Londo, but she was worshipped in Drangleic by the events of *Dark Souls II*, and by *Dark Souls III*, her cult is prominent in the reformed Way of White.
Yorshka, Priscilla's daughter and the younger half-sister of Gwyndolin from another father. She originated in the Painted World of Ariamis, but by the events of *Dark Souls III* has traveled to Irithyll and met her brother, who deified her and made her part of the Way of White's pantheon. It is unclear what she is the Goddess of, although she inherited Gwyndolin's rule of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Stray Demon
snippet:
Stray Demon -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Stray Demon is a greater demon spawned from the Bed of Chaos, the entity that appeared following the attempt of the Witch of Izalith to make a power similar to the First Flame using her Lord Soul. The attempt was successful and she create the Flame of Chaos but Izalith and her powerful soul became a seedbed for a new lifeform: the mother and source of all demons. After its birth, the Stray Demon managed to survive the war that the Silver Knights of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight waged against its kind and at some point it was able to escape from the ruins of Lost Izalith. The demon wandered Lordran until it came to reside in the Northern Undead Asylum, the prison designed to keep Undead locked away from the rest of the world until the end of time, and that became its domain.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

title: Flame God Flann
snippet:
Flame God Flann -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Flann is one of the members of Gwyn's clan who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshiped by the humans as the flame god.

After Lord Gwyn linked the First Flame and his firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, Flann abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities and moved to an unknown location in the world of men, which eventually led him to marry Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight. With her, he'd sire an unknown number of children of divine lineage, continuing the royal family's bloodline.

title: Gods
snippet:
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley, a direct descendant of Gwynevere, possibly her daughter. She was reduced to a life of servitude by Sulyvahn, becoming one of his Boreal Knights.
Gertrude, the "Heavenly Daughter", a maiden of Gwynevere when the latter was Queen of Lothric, believed to be Gwynevere daughter. Although she may not have been revered as a Goddess, she was the central figure of an "Angelic faith" once prominent in Lothric. According to her scriptures, Gertrude was visited by an Angel who imparted to her truths that contradicted the teachings of the Old Gods; because this new faith was heretical to the Way of White, Gertrude was imprisoned in the cell positioned high above the Grand Archives, where she likely died, and part of her scriptures were labelled heretical. It is unclear if the Angels spoken about in her tales are connected to the "Angel" beings born of the fermented humanity of the pilgrims of Londor.

title: Witch's Locks
snippet:
Witch's Locks -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description 
 description : A whip fashioned from the black hair of a daughter of the Witch of Izalith, creator of the Flame of Chaos.

The long, shining locks woven together to create this whip are imbued with the essence of fire, which can be channeled through the use of its Skill.

Skill: Flame Whip
Temporarily coat the whip in fire, the self-same fire as that which consumed the Witch herself, it is said.

title: Salaman the Master Pyromancer
snippet:
Salaman the Master Pyromancer -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Salaman was from an era two hundred years before the events that transpired in Lordran with the arrival of the Chosen Undead. He was the first to meet Quelana of Izalith after her self-imposed exile from her homeland. He was capable of seeing her and was thus allowed to learn her pyromancy, becoming Master Pyromancer in the world of men.

He also came to be known by the title "Great Fireball", referring to the pyromancy of the same name which he ostensibly used often, learned from Quelana herself. He would later pass on his knowledge to his own pupil, Carmina, who pushed pyromancy towards a new direction.

title: Gertrude
snippet:
Gertrude -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Gertrude was the holy maiden of the Queen of Lothric, who was said to be her mother. She taught her healing miracle to the knights of the kingdom, and they became part of the miracles in use in Lothric, implying that she had great influence on the Lothric army and clergy.

title: Undead
snippet:
Undead -  Dark Souls - mechanic - causes 
 causes : The curse of undeath was created when Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Ruler of the Age of Fire, began to feel threatened by the descendants of the Furtive Pygmy: humans were immortal beings, born from the Dark yet able to live in a world enlightened by the Fire, whose souls did not lose power despite being endlessly split and multiplied. According to the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the gods were intimidated by this unexplored potential of the Dark Soul. They had briefly glimpsed at the smidgen of life emanated from the primordial human knights, and feared the eventual overthrow of Anor Londo and its Age of Fire. Therefore, a complex and ingenious apparatus was set in motion with the goal to mould humanity into a subservient, weak people that would not only serve the Age of Fire, but also refused to relinquish it to make way for the Age of Dark.

title: Archtree
snippet:
Archtree -  Dark Souls - storyline - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the First Flame ignited itself within an Archtree. In fact, the Kiln of the First Flame, which in Dark Souls was covered by the layers of structures in Dark Souls III appears clearly, revealing that the First Flame was stored exactly in the center of an ancient archtree. Additionally, Izalith created her own copy of the First Flame within the archtree at the center of her city, thus in a likely attempt to replicate the original conditions in which the Flame had manifested itself for her experiment.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - firelinking_duty 
 firelinking_duty : The tradition of linking the Flame plays a central role in Lothric, testified by the Firelink Shrine's location just outside the city walls, connected to the Royal Gardens. A large number of people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual initiated by Lord Gwyn's sacrifice. Those who failed, becoming the Unkindled, were buried near the Shrine in the Cemetery of Ash. Next to the Cemetery was an arena complete with stands, where Iudex Gundyr's golem judged those who aspired to become Lords, testing their strength. The ritual of the linking of the Flame permeated the kingdom at every level up to the royal family, who were obsessed with producing a worthy Champion in their line to preserve their divine mandate as the guardians of the Age of Fire.

title: Goddess Fina
snippet:
Goddess Fina -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Fina is one of the members of Gwyn's clan who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. She was worshiped by the humans as a goddess, but her domain is not explicitly stated. She was known for possessing a "fateful beauty" and for the fact that her love, protection and favor were all as fickle as the weather. Her blessed rings reflect this, as they break beyond repair if they are ever taken off.

title: Filianore
snippet:
Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Filianore is the last daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Her sacred symbol is a crest of young grass.

She did not reside in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire unlike the other deities. Her father Gwyn, after winning the war against the dragons, "gave" Filianore as a gift to the Pygmy Lords together with a magnificent ringed city at the edge of the world. Before leaving her in the Ringed City, Gwyn promised her that he would come back for her some day.

Throughout the millennia that followed in the Age of Fire, the Pygmies worshipped Filianore as a goddess, building a church in her name with her as the matriarch. Even the Pygmy Lords who possessed the Dark Soul and ruled the city relied on her for salvation.

title: Asylum Demon
snippet:
Asylum Demon -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Asylum Demon is a lesser demon spawned from the Bed of Chaos, the entity that appeared following the attempt of the Witch of Izalith to make a power similar to the First Flame using her Lord Soul. The attempt was successful and she create the Flame of Chaos but Izalith and her powerful soul became a seedbed for a new lifeform: the mother and source of all demons. After its birth, the Asylum Demon managed to survive the war that the Silver Knights of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight waged against its kind and at some point it was able to escape from the ruins of Lost Izalith, bringing its Demon's Great Hammer, made from the stone archtrees, with it. The demon wandered Lordran until it came to reside in the Northern Undead Asylum, the prison designed to keep Undead locked away from the rest of the world until the end of time, and that became its domain.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. By this time, the notion that Hollows were the "true face of man" had become more accepted, propagated especially by the Pilgrims of Londor, melding the two titles of Dark Lord into

Summons a fire-spitting chaos orb.

title: Sweet Shalquoir
snippet:
Sweet Shalquoir -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Shalquoir is ancient, possibly predating the Age of Fire. Though most of her allusions are vague, she has several insights into the role of fate and history, with her comments possibly relating to Seath the Scaleless and even making references to the Lost Sinner, The Rotten, and the Ancient Dragon.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Lucatiel was born into a family of peasants in Mirrah, an unprivileged part of the society of this kingdom. In order to ensure the well-being of her family, Lucatiel and her older brother joined the army. At an early age, she and her brother took up fencing together and, eventually, Lucatiel's skills on the battlefield allowed her to become a knightess of the Order.

Although Lucatiel was a skilled combatant, she was no match for her brother. She claims that her brother was a far better swordsman than she was, as she was never able to defeat him. At some point in her life, her brother disappeared without a trace. Lucatiel thought that he might have fallen victim to the undead curse.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Due to the danger that her new faith posed to the kingdom, and despite her close position to the Queen, Gertrude was imprisoned in the ceiling cell inside the Grand Archives. Here she was subjected to the experiments of scholars, who also toyed with her sacred chime, using the power of crystals to make a catalyst that was suitable for casting both miracles and sorceries. Eventually the abuses of the scholars led Gertrude to lose her voice and her sight, but she remained determined to write down the story of the Angel, even if in the form of incoherent scrawls.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Lucatiel's summon sign appears even if she has disappeared from the game.
In her concept artwork, it was revealed that Lucatiel's original weapon of choice was a thrusting sword similar to Chancellor Wellager's Espada Ropera.
Initially, when the first renders and screenshots of Lucatiel were revealed, many fans believed Lucatiel to be male. Her actual gender wasn't known until her voice was heard in-game.
Despite her weapon being classified as a Greatsword, Lucatiel wields her weapon like a straight sword.
Director Yui Tanimura revealed in an interview that Lucatiel was supposed to be a Don Quixote-like character and used to be accompanied by the Bell Keeper of Alken who originally had the role of his Sancho Panza. The idea was scrapped and the original face was repurposed as the iconic mask she now wears.

title: Black Knight
snippet:
Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : In *Dark Souls: The Age of Fire*, it is revealed that the Black Knight in the Northern Undead Asylum is actually what remains of the protagonist of the comic series, Silver Knight Arkon.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet:
Allfather Lloyd -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Lloyd is one of the members of Gwyn's clan who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshiped by the humans as a god presiding over law and caste, and his face was even minted on the gold coins used by men. He is likely one of the primordial humanoids that appeared underground after the First Flame came to be, as he was a uncle to Gwyn, thus born before him. He was the younger brother of one of his parents.

title: Gold-Hemmed Black Gloves
snippet:

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Another common strategy is to summon one or two phantoms and position both next to each orb, with the host out of reach of the Bed of Chaos' arm sweeps, but in a direct line towards the entrance to the core. After both phantoms break the orbs, the host can then head to the entrance of its mouth and kill the boss.
A simple solo strategy involves "corpse-running" to the fog door and then running to each orb and then to the Bed of Chaos itself. Some players prefer to stay hollowed so that humanity is not wasted, since many deaths may follow after the first orb breaks.
Players with a high number of Humanities or souls may be interested in investing in some Rings of Sacrifice.
The chaos scythe/fire pick(s) attacks will almost always miss unless the player stays in one spot for too long.
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
The greatest concerns to the player over the encounter will be dealing with the boss' broad, sweeping attacks and the large, bottomless holes that open in different parts of the arena.
Once both roots have been cut, the player must reach the boss' heart to access and kill the Chaos Bug, however it is important to be aware that directly in front of the boss is a large bottomless hole. The primary way across is a wide branch that runs from the boss toward where the encounter begins, just below the height of the floor.
A relatively safe method of dealing with both attacks and holes is to hug the walls around the outside of the arena, on the ledges behind the holes and out of reach of the boss (though, not the Volcanic Chaos attack, see below). From here, the player may sprint and jump to cross the holes and reach the orbs if their weight is low enough, or attack the branches and roots from range with magic or a bow.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Unlike most boss encounters, the goal here is not to whittle away the boss's health, but to strike at three vulnerable nodes. Thus, the difficulty in defeating this boss mostly lies in discovering the points to strike while avoiding being knocked in a hole rather than in defeating the boss via conventional methods.
The vulnerable nodes are two roots within glowing spheres, visible to the right and left of the boss at the start of the encounter, and the Chaos Bug within this boss' heart. Striking the roots expands the boss' list of available attacks and 'unlocks' access to the boss' heart.
It is also noteworthy that progress made in damaging one or both of the roots does not reset upon the player's death, allowing repeated attempts at the boss to add incremental progress to the encounter.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.
Magic Shield and Strong Magic Shield can be extremely useful against Bed of Chaos, as they can easily block both the scythe and swiping attack with a medium shield without breaking player's guard. This creates a relatively long opening and player can use the remaining stamina to quickly run towards the heart/orb and deal the fatal blow. Lingering Dragoncrest Ring is recommended to counter the short duration of both spells.
One last potential strategy involves the use of shields with high stability. By two-handing a shield such as Havel's Greatshield, and with sufficient Stamina, a player can become almost completely immune to both the damage and knockback effects of the Bed of Chaos's sweeping attacks.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : A relatively easy way to beat this boss is to be human and summon Maneater Mildred, whose summon sign is right outside the Fog Door. Let Mildred distract Quelaag and stay away from her lava attack, as this is certain death. When away from her, pick off her health with ranged attacks, while Mildred tanks. This way Quelaag should be dead within a short period of time.

Another easy way to kill her is to get any halberd with a vertical light attack, such as the Great Scythe or Gargoyle's Halberd, and then repeatedly hitting Quelaag's human part. When aimed properly, she will stagger every time the attack connects, interrupting whatever she's doing. This can be repeated to prevent her from attacking at all.

There is a spot between the stairs on the far side of the arena and the wall where Quelaag is unable to reach the player, at which point she can safely be killed from a distance using ranged attacks.

**Another possible inspiration is [https://forgottenrealms.wikia.com/wiki/Lolth Lolth the Spider-Queen], a half-spider demon goddess in *Dungeons & Dragons* canon. She is first encountered in the 1978 adventure module *Vault of the Drow*. Like Quelaag, Lolth rules over a subterranean domain.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: However the flames of Chaos would not be sated, and over time the Ivory Knight was drained of his vigour and, sensing the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. However he was devoured by the chaos, becoming an empty husk controlled by it. After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery but their souls too were corrupted by the flames, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being. They were then driven only by the urge of expunging any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots.
